hints: A subtree rooted at u is a contiguous region in a DFS preorder numbering.
Store each node's value at its preorder position; subtree u occupies [tin[u],tout[u]].
A Fenwick tree supports point updates and subtree sum queries.
analogy: Flatten the tree so all descendants of a node occupy one continuous slice of an array.
example: If node 2's DFS interval is positions 3..6, its subtree sum is the Fenwick range sum over that interval.
algorithm: Euler-tour DFS assigns tin and tout. Put values at tin positions; update a node's position and query prefix(tout)-prefix(tin-1).
correctness: DFS enters a node before all its descendants and leaves only after them, so the subtree maps to exactly that preorder interval.
complexity: O((n+q) log n) time and O(n) space.
